facts.raw_span: a three-week history of a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump
a low-grade fever (37.5–38°C) for one week
hypertension—treated with lacidipine, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide
a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass performed two years earlier
lost 112 kg (BMI from 64.6 to 28 kg/m2)
smoked 30 cigarettes daily
took vitamin (A, D, E, B complex), calcium, cholecalciferol, and iron supplements
a tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla

laboratory studies—including a complete blood count, ESR, liver and renal panels, autoantibodies (ANA, RF), complement levels, inflammatory markers, thyroid function, and serologies for a broad spectrum of viral and parasitic pathogens—were all normal or negative
a thoracoabdominal CT scan was unremarkable except for the axillary lymphadenopathy
a biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
an investigation for mycobacteria was negative
